Annual Report of the Bank for the Financial Year 2025-26  
 
Pursuant to Regulation 34(1) and other applicable provisions of the SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we submit the Annual 
Report of the Bank for the FY  2025-26 including Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Report (BRSR), along with Notice of 71st Annual General Meeting (AGM) 
of the Bank  scheduled to be held on Thursday, 18th June, 2026 at 03:00 PM (IST) 
through Video Conferencing (VC) / Other Audio-Visual Means (OAVM). 
In terms of relaxation granted by Ministry of Corporate Affairs and Securities and 
Exchange Board of India through their respective Circulars, regarding the requirement 
to send physical copy of the annual report and notice of AGM to shareholders, the 
Annual Report for FY  2025-26 including BRSR and the Notice of 71st AGM is sent 
through electronic mode to those shareholders whose e-mail addresses are registered 
with the Registrar and Transfer Agent / Depositories. 
The Annual Report for FY2025-26 can be accessed as under: 
Link for Annual Report 2025-26 QR code for Annual Report 2025-26 
https://sbi.bank.in/web/corporate-
governance/annual-report- 
 
 
Yours faithfully,

By embracing a digital-first mindset, we 
leverage advanced technology to create a 
purpose-led, innovation-centric ecosystem 
designed to serve the customers better. At the 
same time, we remain steadfastly committed 
to partnering India in its journey of economic 
resilience and long-term progress.
We have defined our business ethos as a 
holistic strategy driving inclusive growth. 
Keeping customers at the centre of our 
strategic approach, we focus on elevating 
their banking experience – making it faster, 
simpler, convenient, and more accessible.
Our integrated, hyperpersonal approach, 
which combines trust with scale and 
technology, ensures that every solution is 
designed to meet the evolving needs of 
customers, in both urban and rural areas. 
Data-driven personalisation enables us to 
simplify the complexity of banking, helping to 
drive financial democratisation and inclusion 
for more and more Indians aspiring for better 
lives and a brighter future.
A Smart Bank for a Digital India 
State Bank of India (SBI) is powering the nation’s digital journey with a comprehensive 
suite of innovative products and services. With customer-centric offerings designed 
to cater to all segments, we are at the forefront of the transformation that is driving 
smart banking to enhance customer ease and convenience. 
SBI at a Glance
We continue to scale the banking experience of our customers through an extensive network 
of branches and ATMs and a growing digital presence. Driven by our aim to offer responsible 
and sustainable banking solutions, we stand out today as the trusted and preferred banking 
partner for over 53 crore Indians.
Rooted in a heritage going 
back over 200 years and 
headquartered in Mumbai 
(Maharashtra), SBI 
continues to dominate the 
Indian banking landscape, 
going beyond traditional 
mass retail to deliver to 
diverse financial needs  
of its customers.

Annual Report 2025-26
Your Bank had successfully raised ₹25,000 crore through a QIP, which is the largest ever in the 
history of the Indian capital market, marked by a memorable Bell Ringing Ceremony held at 
NSE Mumbai on 23 July 2025. This landmark equity raise reflects the faith of investors across 
the globe in SBI’s strong fundamentals and the Indian economy, as supported by the fact that 
more than 64% of the participation/bids came from foreign investors.

11
Company Overview Responsible Approach Governance Statutory Reports Financial Statements
Expanding reach
The International Banking-Domestic (IBD) department serves 
as a single point of contact between the domestic and foreign 
offices in areas related to Trade Finance and International 
Banking. It aims at improving synergies and trade flows 
between domestic and foreign offices, correspondent banks, 
and the trading community, by acting as a robust link between 
them. IBD facilitates growth of export credit by actively 
engaging branches, trade bodies, and other stakeholders.
Building a global banking footprint
SBI embarked on its international journey with the opening 
of its first international operations in Colombo (Sri Lanka) in 
1864. Over a century and a half down the line, today, SBI has 
245 overseas points of presence spread across 29 countries. 
These foreign branches are active on both assets and 
liabilities side, with specialised branches for Retail Banking, 
Corporate Banking, Trade Finance business and Investments. 
Your Bank has 5 central treasuries to manage funds and ALM 
for the offices associated with them. Furthermore, YONO 
Global, your Banks’ digital banking app, is enabled across 
all 14 centres, supporting retail operations. Your Bank has 
also collaborated with Fintechs, exchange companies, 
and maintains correspondent relations with 222 banks in  
56 countries worldwide. 
Drawing on a legacy in global banking that dates back to 1864, SBI plays an 
active role in advancing India’s growing presence worldwide. We partner with 
Indian businesses and individuals overseas as a reliable financial ally, while also 
strengthening our connections within the markets we operate in.

14
Annual Report 2025-26
Dear Shareholders,
ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
The financial year gone by unfolded against a backdrop of 
heightened geopolitical tensions, evolving trade dynamics, 
and persistent global economic uncertainty. The Global 
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth is projected to 
slow down, largely on account of the West Asia conflict. 
Elevated public debt, volatile energy prices, and increasing 
geopolitical fragmentation continue to pose risks to 
long-term global growth.
Against this backdrop, India remained the fastest-growing 
major economy in the world. Real GDP is estimated to grow 
by 7.6% during the year. Strong domestic demand, sustained 
public investment, improving private consumption, and policy 
continuity supported economic momentum during the year.  
India’s macroeconomic fundamentals remain robust, with 
inflation likely to remain within the RBI’s comfort band and 
fiscal policy maintaining a prudent balance between growth 
and consolidation. The recent challenges posed by West 
Asia conflict are proactively being accommodated through 
regulatory dispensation by the RBI and fiscal measures and 
derisking through ECLGS 5.0 rolled out by the Government of 
India.  However, the economic fallout of the conflict may lead 
to lower GDP growth and higher inflation in FY 2027.
YOUR BANK’S PERFORMANCE
The last financial year was a landmark year for your Bank. 
Building on the momentum of previous years, we strengthened 
our market leadership across key business segments while 
continuing our transformation into a technology-driven, 
customer-centric financial institution.
Your Bank’s balance sheet crossed ₹76 lakh crore during the 
year, while total business surpassed ₹109 lakh crore, reflecting 
the scale, strength, and trust reposed in us by millions of 
customers across the country and globally.
Deposit Growth
Deposits grew by 11.03% to ₹59.76 lakh crore, supported by 
strong growth in both domestic and overseas operations. 
CASA deposits which grew by 9.53% to ₹22.62 lakh crore, 
continued to remain a key strength of the Bank, with savings 
bank deposits recording the highest growth in the last 
four years. Your Bank’s CASA ratio stood at 39.46% as of 
March 2026. 
Our strong liability franchise remains a reflection of the  
deep trust reposed in the Bank by millions of customers across 
the country.
Advances Growth
Your Bank’s advances registered a strong growth of 16.87% 
to ₹49.33 lakh crore, driven by healthy expansion across retail, 
agriculture, SME, and corporate segments. 
Retail advances crossed the milestone of ₹17 lakh crore 
during the year, while our housing loan portfolio which is 
steadily approaching ₹10 lakh crore, continued to strengthen 
its market leadership position. Agriculture lending crossed 
₹4 lakh crore, the highest for any bank in India, reaffirming 
our commitment to supporting rural prosperity and inclusive 
economic development.
Having exceeded ₹6 lakh crore, the SME portfolio registered 
strong growth during the year, supported by focused initiatives 
towards supply chain finance, cash-flow-based lending,  
and digital credit delivery. Our corporate portfolio which 
clocked double digit growth reaching over ₹14 lakh crore, 
continued to remain well diversified and positively skewed 
towards higher-rated borrowers, reflecting our disciplined 
underwriting standards.
Investment
Your Bank’s total investment book increased to ₹18.09 lakh 
crore, as of March 2026, of which 95.48% are domestic 
investments. 73.95% of the domestic investments are under 
HTM category. The yield on investments was 7.01%. 
Profitability
Your Bank continued to deliver strong profitability in FY 2026. 
Standalone operating profit touched ₹1.23 lakh crore, with a 
YoY growth of 11.25%, while standalone net profit grew by 
12.88% to ₹80,032 crore. Net Interest Income (NII) of your 
Bank grew by 4.08% to ₹1.73 lakh crore in FY 2026, while the 
cost-to-income ratio improved further to 50.11% from 51.64% 
last year. 
Return on Assets (RoA) improved to 1.12% in FY 2026, against 
1.10% for FY 2025. Return on Equity (RoE) at 18.57% for  
FY 2026 continued to create long-term value for stakeholders.
Dividend
I am happy to announce that the Central Board of your Bank 
has declared a dividend of ₹17.35 per equity share for the 
financial year ended March 31, 2026.
₹109 lakh crore 
Total Business crossed in FY 2026
15
Company Overview Responsible Approach Governance Statutory Reports Financial Statements
Capital
The capital ratios of your Bank continued to improve during 
the financial year. During the year, the Bank successfully 
raised ₹25,000 crore of equity capital through Qualified 
Institutional Placement, strengthening our Tier-I capital base 
and enhancing our ability to support future growth.
Our CET-1 ratio improved substantially, registering 
the highest ever level of 12.29% and the overall Capital 
Adequacy Ratio at 15.40% remained comfortably above 
regulatory requirement.
Asset Quality
Equally encouraging has been the continued improvement 
in asset quality. Gross NPA declined to 1.49%, recording an 
improvement of 33 bps (YoY), while Net NPA at 0.39% improved 
by 8 bps YoY.  The slippage ratio was contained at 0.54% and 
the Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) stood at 74.36% without 
AUCA and 99.01% with AUCA as of March 2026. 
These outcomes reflect our sustained focus on prudent 
underwriting, portfolio monitoring, and responsible growth.
Customer Experience and Centricity
At the heart of our strategy lies an unwavering commitment to 
customer centricity. Serving over 53 crore customers through 
an extensive network of more than 23,000 branches, over 
65,000 ATMs, digital channels, and nearly 80,000 customer 
service points (CSPs), we continue to focus on making 
banking simpler, faster, more accessible, and more responsive 
to evolving customer expectations.
FY 2026 saw significant progress in strengthening customer 
experience across delivery channels. We established the 
Centre of Excellence for Refinement of User Experience 
(CRUX), expanded customer engagement initiatives across 
circles, and enhanced multilingual accessibility across service 
platforms for wider reach and convenience. 
We also introduced robust mechanisms to measure customer 
satisfaction and continuously improve service quality. 
Customer Satisfaction Score and Customer Effort Score were 
measured by an external agency through incognito visits 
across ~4,000 branches and were estimated at 3.62 out of 4 
and 6.74 out of 7, respectively for FY 2026. 
Technology and Innovation
Technology continues to be a defining pillar of your Bank’s 
transformation journey. Digital adoption across channels 
has reached unprecedented scale, with alternate channels 
accounting for nearly 99% of transactions during the year. 
Our leadership across ATMs, debit card spends, and mobile 
The launch of YONO 2.0 marked 
a significant step forward in 
delivering hyper-personalised 
and seamless digital experiences. 
With over 10 crore registered 
users, YONO continues to redefine 
customer engagement and digital 
banking in India. 
banking transactions reflects the scale and maturity of our 
digital ecosystem. 
YONO, our flagship digital platform, continued to evolve into a 
comprehensive financial and lifestyle ecosystem. The launch 
of YONO 2.0 marked a significant step forward in delivering 
hyper-personalised and seamless digital experiences. 
With over 10 crore registered users, YONO continues to 
redefine customer engagement and digital banking in India. 
With the introduction of an enterprise-wide MarTech stack in 
YONO, we now deliver hyper-personalised offerings across 
all customer personas. In addition to elevated experience of 
retail customers, the platform also supports around 44 lakh 
corporates with 59 lakh users. 
Project SARAL, our Operations Process Re-engineering 
initiative, marked an important structural reset during the 
year. With the launch of the first wave of identified themes, the 
initiative seeks to challenge legacy constructs and reimagine 
the Bank through the lens of simplicity, agility, and customer 
centricity. Key initiatives undertaken include Universal Branch 
Access, aimed at dismantling the traditional “home branch” 
mindset and enabling seamless banking access across 
branches; implementation of Single KYC across products to 
simplify customer onboarding and servicing; and automation 
of back-office processes such as inward clearing through the 
use of Generative AI. 
These initiatives are expected to significantly improve 
operational efficiency and enhance overall customer 
experience.

Financial inclusion remains central to our institutional 
mission. Through our extensive Business Correspondent 
and CSP network, we continue to extend banking access 
to underserved and remote areas of the country. The Bank

Strategic New Initiatives
Your Bank continued to undertake several strategic 
initiatives aligned with India’s evolving economic priorities 
and the broader vision of Viksit Bharat. During the year, we 
strengthened our capabilities across supply chain finance, 
digital lending, international banking, green finance, and SME 
ecosystem financing, with a focus on making banking more 
accessible, efficient, and future-ready.
As India accelerates its transition towards a low-carbon 
economy, the Bank remains committed to supporting 
sustainable growth and climate-focused financing. 
During FY 2026, we expanded our green lending portfolio 
across renewable energy, electric mobility, biofuels, and 
climate technologies. Further strengthening our sustainability 
agenda, the Bank introduced CHAKRA, a dedicated knowledge 
and financing platform aimed at supporting emerging 
climate-focused and future-ready sectors.
To bring focused attention towards strengthening our liability 
franchise and improving CASA mobilisation, the Bank 
institutionalised a simple yet powerful discipline — ABCD: 
All Branches to Contribute to Deposits, with the philosophy 
that every branch, irrespective of size or geography, has an 
important role in expanding our deposit base. This broad-based 
participation is expected to further strengthen the resilience, 
granularity, and sustainability of deposit growth.
Your Bank has a clear aspiration to emerge as India’s leading 
wealth architect. We have launched SBI Premier (Virtual 
Relationship Managers) to deliver a virtual yet personalised 
servicing experience to Premier segment customers, effectively 
overcoming geographical barriers, especially in remote and 
underserved areas. Our overall Wealth Hub network has 
increased to 344 across 173 centres nationwide. This expanded 
footprint reflects your Bank’s commitment towards building 
a strong, customer-centric wealth management franchise 
founded on trust, relationship strength, and comprehensive 
financial solutions.
In retail banking, the Bank launched a web-based home 
loan application platform that enables customers to apply 
seamlessly from anywhere and receive instant in-principle 
approvals.
To deepen our SME engagement, the Bank established Supply 
Chain Finance CPCs across all circles to improve delivery 
efficiency and accelerate credit access. In addition, a cash 
flow-based lending product leveraging UPI settlement data 
was launched for existing CASA customers, with a special 
focus on supporting Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs).
Your Bank has set up an MSME Centre of Excellence at 
Gurugram which will serve as a national knowledge platform, 
integrating sectoral research, ecosystem collaboration, fintech 
experimentation, and policy advocacy. We want this CoE to 
become a nerve-centre for capacity building, innovation, and 
thought leadership in MSME banking.
Your Bank has also established an integrated IT & Digital 
Audit Unit which will ensure that the IT infrastructure and 
digital offerings are secure and meet regulatory standards. 
The unit will also cover audit of digital products, processes, 
models and logs thereby strengthening the existing IS  
Audit Framework.

Corporate Social Responsibility
Your Bank has been undertaking Corporate Social 
Responsibility (CSR) since 1973 and has formalised CSR 
with the establishment of the SBI Foundation, through which 
it provides opportunities to uplift the socio-economic status 
of marginalised communities.
In FY 2026, the Bank spent over ₹700 crore on CSR, through 
1,529 activities undertaken across India covering 20,000 
villages. CSR focus areas include Healthcare and Sanitation, 
Education, Empowerment of Women and Senior Citizens, 
Environment, Protection of National Heritage among others.
Subsidiaries
As on March 2026, your Bank had 26 subsidiaries operating 
across diverse business lines. The Bank’s subsidiaries 
delivered strong performance in insurance, mutual funds, 
cards, investment banking, and rural banking businesses, 
reinforcing the strength and diversity of the SBI Group 
franchise.
SBI Life Insurance Company Limited ranks first amongst the 
private life insurers. SBI General Insurance Company Limited 
with a major presence in personal accident segment and crop 
segment stands fifth amongst the private players.
SBI Cards and Payment Services Limited is the No. 2 player in 
Cards and No. 3 in Spends. SBI Funds Management Limited 
(SBIMF) is the largest player in the mutual funds market.
Your Bank has sponsored nine regional rural banks (RRBs) 
across nine states.
The net profit of SBI Group, combining all the subsidiaries 
reached ₹83,299 crore, increasing by 7.40% over the  
previous year.

Prioritising Sustainable National 
Development 
The responsible growth strategy at State Bank of India (SBI) extends beyond 
business imperatives to include sustainability as a key tenet. As active partners 
in India’s sustainable development journey, we have prioritised environmental, 
social and governance (ESG) as an important pivot of growth. We have integrated 
sustainable practices into the organisation’s systems and processes, in line with our 
commitment to driving environment conservation and resource optimisation. Our 
dedicated ESG and Climate Finance Unit is steering the Bank’s strategic actions, 
aimed at the realisation of our sustainability goals.
Environmental Stewardship
Our key sustainability targets
 Carbon neutrality in our 
internal operations by 2030
 Green portfolio equivalent to 
7.5% of domestic advances  
by 2030
 Net Zero emissions by 2055
To achieve our 2030 carbon 
neutrality targets, we have 
formulated a comprehensive, 
time-bound roadmap with year-
wise emission reduction targets, 
driven by large-scale renewable 
energy usage, energy efficiency 
enhancements, adoption of 
advanced technologies, process 
optimisation, and robust energy 
management systems.''

Annual Report 2025-26
Scaling sustainable growth
A series of initiatives and milestone achievements helped 
strengthen Bank's sustainable development agenda during  
FY 2025-26. We integrated ESG considerations more deeply 
into our business operations while enhancing our focus on 
climate-aligned financing of green and sustainable projects.
Key highlights
 Green Advanced portfolio grew 111.56% to cross the  
₹1 trillion mark
 Mobilised Green Liabilities at 18.94% of Green advances 
from Green Sources like Green LoCs / Green Bonds / 
BGTLs / Green Deposits
 Raised Green Bonds of USD 1,050 million and Bilateral 
Green Term loan of EURO 300 million till date
 Availed Lines of Credit (LoCs) aggregating to approx. 
USD 3,596 million to fund projects driving a positive 
environmental and social impact
 Raised ₹189.08 crore till March 2026 under Green Deposit 
products as part of RBI’s Policy on Climate Finance and 
Management of Climate Change Risks
 Streamlined financing for solar projects catering to SMEs 
and businesses through our dedicated Surya Shakti Cell
 Achieved over 34.69 MW of installed solar rooftop 
capacity across our branches and ATMs
 Expanded green power procurement through green tariff 
mechanisms to 361 offices across various states
 Transitioned 117 offices/buildings in Green Buildings – 6 
buildings certified as Net Zero and 111 certified under 
various categories (Platinum/Gold/Silver) by Indian 
Green Building Council (IGBC)
Other initiatives
 Launched “Solar Sakhi’ as a training and capacity building 
programme for women beneficiaries of PM Surya Ghar 
scheme, with support from the Asian Development Bank 
(ADB), to maintain rooftop solar installations
 Conducted regular workshops and knowledge 
sessions in the areas of ESG/Green Reporting, carbon 
accounting, climate finance, and sustainable lending 
frameworks, etc.
Launch of Green Club initiative
We have introduced ‘Green Club’ initiative as a 
strategic move aimed at institutionalising the best 
practices towards carbon neutrality in our internal 
operations. Measurable and non-measurable metrics 
have been established to map the performance of 
the Green Club units.
In an endorsement of its sustained 
leadership in advancing sustainable 
finance, SBI received the inaugural 
“WSBI-ESBG SDG Award 2025” in 
Washington DC and the “Excellence 
in Sustainable & Responsible 
Banking” award at the 7th ET BFSI 
Exceller Awards 2025."

Upgrading societal infrastructure 
We undertook a series of infrastructure development  
projects during the year to upgrade primary schools, 
old-age homes and women shelters, as well as orphanages 
and special schools, across the country. We also upgraded 
Anganwadi centres, and constructed and repaired toilet 
complexes in schools under the Prime Minister’s 
Beti Bachao 
Beti Padhao Campaign. 
Providing aid to armed forces veterans
Continuing with our support for armed forces veterans, 
we contributed a total of ₹10 crore towards the Armed 
Forces Flag Day Fund (AFFDF) to support the education 
of dependent children of armed forces veterans. Since  
FY 2021-22, a total collection of ₹50 crore has helped 
contribute significantly to preparing such children for a 
brighter future.
Supporting schools in Karnataka
During the year, SBI supported schools operated by the 
Sri Sringeri Sharada Peetham Charitable Trust in Sringeri, 
Karnataka, with a donation of ₹99.06 lakh. The aid benefited 
children studying in the Mutt-operated schools through 
purchase of five school buses. 
Strengthening healthcare & sanitation 
facilities
Aligned with our commitment to promoting healthcare and 
sanitation facilities, we provided ₹1.30 crore to the Varanasi 
Nagar Nigam for installation of a Garbage Disposal Station 
in Varanasi city of Uttar Pradesh. The initiative was part of 
our efforts to promote a clean and healthy environment in 
the region. We also distributed sanitary pads to girls across 
schools in several states. 
Generating livelihood for the poor
SBI manages 164 Rural Self-Employment Training Institutes 
(RSETIs) across 29 States/UTs, out of a total of 615 RSETIs 
sponsored by all banks in the country. In FY 2025-26, we 
sponsored RSETIs with a CSR fund of ₹25.53 crore to 
facilitate construction and other essential facilities. Our other 
key livelihood generation initiatives included ₹200 lakh for 
the Uttar Pradesh State Government Zero Poverty initiative, 
and ₹49.20 lakh to empower poor fishermen in P. M. Lanka 
village in West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh.

Digitising international operations
In FY 2025-26, we launched the first phase of Project KENTRO 
at six foreign offices – London, Dubai, Gift City, Antwerp, Male 
and Johannesburg – with the aim to centralise and digitise 
trade finance back-office operations. The operations have 
been shifted to Hyderabad and Kolkata, enabling automation 
and paperless processing. The project will be implemented 
across all our foreign offices by the end of June 2026.
We also kickstarted the implementation of a Supply Chain 
Financing platform – titled ‘Global SCF Link’ – with a pilot at 
the New York office. The initiative will be rolled out across all 
FOs in FY 2026-27.

strengthened our digital outreach in FY 2025-26. As of

Your Bank have adopted the Accessibility Standards and Guidelines for the Banking

India’s directives under the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1), have been 
incorporated across YONO Business Desktop/Web and the YONO Business Mobile App.
Special facilities for PwDs in  
Debit Cards:
Braille Debit Card: Committed to 
inclusive banking, the Bank has rolled out 
Braille Debit Card – a product designed to 
empower visually impaired customers and 
strengthen our leadership in accessibility.
The Braille Debit Card is a strategic lever 
for inclusion and brand differentiation. 
By addressing accessibility gaps, we not 
only enhance customer trust but also 
create long-term value for stakeholders.

The Business Correspondent channel serves as a critical bridge for financial 
inclusion, currently operating through 79,000+ pan-India outlets. Implementation of  
specific infrastructure and technology upgrades are further advancing our commitment to 
serving PwDs.
1.  Infrastructure & Mobility Support
a. Most CSP outlets are strategically located on ground 
floors to ensure ease of access.
b. 100% paperless account opening and transaction 
services through TAB devices have been implemented, 
enabling persons with disabilities to not only open 
accounts but also transact from the comfort of  
their homes.
2.  Technological Inclusivity
a. Voice prompts have been integrated into the 
transaction flow to enhance accessibility for all 
customers, particularly the visually challenged. 
The feature is available in 10 regional languages 
and provides audible confirmation of transactions, 
ensuring financial autonomy for visually impaired 
users.
b. Face authentication has been introduced for AePS 
transactions via android tablets. This enables elderly 
or disabled customers with worn or damaged 
fingerprints to easily access their accounts, while 
promoting a hygienic, contactless process.

43

Global Economic Scenario
The global economy has entered a critical phase in 2026, with 
the sudden outbreak of war in West Asia adversely affecting 
the global growth outlook. Disruption of shipping traffic in the 
Strait of Hormuz, energy price shock, trade disruption, and 
loss of business confidence are some of the key themes that 
have made headlines since February. 
West Asia is a significant producer of ammonia and nitrogen 
- key ingredients in many synthetic fertilisers. Iran is one 
of the largest exporters of methanol while Qatar produces 
around 35% of the world’s helium, used in the production of 
semiconductors. The impact of the conflict is not localised or 
restricted to just energy infrastructure but also affects other 
key industrial intermediate inputs, with wider implications for 
the global economy.
Against this development, the IMF World Economic Outlook 
in April 2026 projected a slowdown in global growth from 
3.4% in 2025 to 3.1% in 2026. The conflicts’ impact is being 
felt across geographies. The Euro Area growth is expected to 
taper from 1.4% in 2025 to 1.1% in 2026. Growth in emerging 
markets is also expected to soften to 3.9% in 2026 from 4.4% in 
2025. The IMF projections are conditional on limited conflict, 
indicating that the growth outlook is tilted to the downside if 
peace talks fall short of expectations. 
The war’s impact on energy prices was immediate. Brent crude 
oil traded at around $110 per barrel at the time this report was 
finalised. The rising commodity prices may result in firmer 
inflation expectations going ahead. Projections for global 
headline inflation stand at 4.4% according to IMF, 52 bps 
higher than its pre-conflict forecast.
The closure of Strait of Hormuz has further impacted global 
trade, already battered by the impact of tariffs in 2025. 
World trade volume growth is expected to decline from 5.1% 
in 2025 to 2.8% in 2026. Export of both goods and services is 
also projected to decline in 2026. 
Economic Backdrop and Banking Environment
India’s Economic Scenario
The Indian economy demonstrated resilience amid trade 
tensions with the US and registered a growth of 7.6% 
in FY 2026, as per the Second Advanced Estimates. 
The manufacturing sector remained a major driver of growth 
in the last two years. Private final consumption expenditure – 
the mainstay of aggregate demand – revived and recorded a 
growth of 7.7% in FY 2026 while gross fixed capital formation 
expanded by 7.1% in FY 2026, higher than 6.4% growth seen 
in FY 2025. The inflationary conditions during FY 2026 also 
remained benign with CPI Inflation registering an average 
growth of 2.1% during the year. Additionally, progress in 
summer crop area coverage remained satisfactory till the end 
of April despite concerns over the potential impact of El-Nino 
on water availability. 
Union Budget 2026-27 continued to focus on reforms in 
agriculture, MSME, investment, and exports, alongside key 
areas such as taxation, power sector, urban development, 
mining, and financial and regulatory sectors, to strengthen 
growth potential and global competitiveness. However, the 
policy calculus could not have anticipated the sudden outbreak 
of war in West Asia. The war resulted in a brief period of LPG 
shortage triggering contingency measures centred around 
energy supplies. Official communications indicate that Indian 
ships have safely passed the Strait of Hormuz but uncertainty 
around ship movements persist. 
The Government, in March 2026, extended the RELIEF 
(Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) 
scheme to support exporters affected by war-related 
disruptions in the Gulf and West Asia. The Reserve Bank of 
India (RBI) has also allowed pre- and post-shipment credit 
of up to 450 days until June 2026. Periodically released 
‘Inter-Ministerial Briefing on Recent Developments in West 
Asia’ indicates the span of policy measures to accommodate 
and absorb the shock. Furthermore, fertiliser availability 
is being ensured, LPG hoarding is being checked and full 
custom duty on select critical petrochemical products is 
being exempted to shield the industry. Moreover, Emergency 
Credit Line Guarantee Scheme 5.0 has also been approved to 
support MSME and airlines sector. 
Currently, the war’s full impact on the Indian economy is 
difficult to quantify owing to uncertainty about its duration. 
However, on the qualitative front, it has possibly impacted 
rice and bananas, engineering goods, and pharmaceuticals 
business. The indirect impact includes reordering of shipping 
routes diverting via the Cape of Good Hope. The Real GDP 
growth for 2026-27 is now projected at 6.9%. 
The Union Budget 2026–27 focused 
on reforms across agriculture, 
MSMEs, investment, exports, and 
key sectors to strengthen growth 
and global competitiveness.
Annual Report 2025-26
44

Banking Business
FY 2026 was a good year for the banking sector. Both public 
sector banks and private sector banks saw healthy business 
growth with the former’s combined net profit reaching  
₹ 1.98 lakh crore in FY 2026. During the period, the 
aggregate advances and deposits registered a y-o-y growth 
of 16.1% and 13.5% respectively, while the credit to deposit 
ratio at system level reached 81.4%. The wedge between 
deposits and credit growth persisted all through the year. 
The health of banking system further improved during  
FY 2026. For public sector banks (PSB) the capital adequacy 
improved in FY 2026. As per audited financial for March 2026 
capital adequacy ratio of PSBs was in the range 15.40% to 
19.78%. In general, there was no significant pressure on asset 
quality and the net NPA of PSBs was in the range 0.13% to 
0.79%. The net interest margins also stayed healthy for PSBs, 
averaging around 3% as of March 2026. 
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), by the end of FY 2026, 
maintained the repo rate at 5.25% while retaining a neutral 
stance. The year witnessed a slew of measures by RBI 
targeting customer protection, deposit insurance, market 
development and strengthening banking regulations. 
Few notable announcements include reviewing of 
non-fund-based facilities by banks, rolling out Expected 
Credit Loss (ECL) framework for provisioning by banks, 
revising Basel framework on Standardised Approach for 
Credit Risk, Risk Based Premium Framework for Deposit 
Insurance, and permitting acquisition financing by banks, 
among others. 
Outlook
FY 2026 was a good year for India and the Indian banking 
sector, although the outbreak of war in West Asia towards 
the close of the financial year somewhat clouded the future 
outlook. Nevertheless, we foresee a robust demand and 
continued momentum in fixed capital formation in FY 2027, 
supported by increased government capital expenditure. 
Accordingly, the macros are expected to evolve along 
anticipated lines in the next financial year. The GDP growth 
is expected at 6.9% as per RBI, which is strong given 
the vulnerabilities in the external sectors. The domestic 
demand continues to be robust. The domestic inflation is 
expected to rise to 4.6% in FY 2027 but is fully aligned with 
RBI mandate. The numbers indicate that interest rates are 
likely to remain steady in the foreseeable future, subject to 
incoming data. 
The banking system is expected to maintain healthy 
momentum, with advances expected to grow between 
13-14% in FY 2027. While we do not expect significant 
pressure on asset quality in FY 2027, a protracted conflict in 
West Asia and a strong El-Nino may affect the sector’s risk 
profile in the current financial year. 
Against this backdrop, your Bank has delivered improved 
performance vis-à-vis last year. The momentum witnessed in 
FY 2025 continued into FY 2026, with your Bank achieving the 
historic milestone of surpassing ₹109 trillion in total business 
in FY 2026. While prudent risk management and healthy 
internal accruals place your Bank in a comfortable position 
to navigate challenges, a digital-first, customer-first approach 
and unwavering commitment for service to the nation will 
continue to remain the guiding light and deliver sustained 
progress in the coming year.

period, the Investments increased by 6.55% to ₹18,01,254 
crore from ₹16,90,573 crore. The major portion of investment 
in the domestic market was in government securities.

dated 22
nd March, 2019 deferred implementation of Ind 
AS till further notice. However, RBI requires all banks to 
submit Proforma Ind AS financial statements every half year. 
Accordingly, your Bank is preparing and submitting the RBI 
Proforma Ind AS financial statements every half year after 
getting approval of the Steering Committee headed by MD 
(R, C & SARG) formed for monitoring of implementation of 
Ind AS in the Bank.

of ₹6,666 crore (as against ₹2,172 crore in FY 2025) was 
transferred to Capital Reserves. No transfer to Investment 
Fluctuation Reserve in FY 2026 and FY 2025.

Retail Loans
Auto Loans
The Indian automobile industry demonstrated resilient growth 
during FY 2025-26. While the first half of the year remained 
relatively muted, reflecting a marginal year-on-year decline 
in sales, the sector witnessed a strong revival in the latter 
half, supported by GST rationalisation. The passenger vehicle 
segment continued to be driven by robust demand for SUVs, 
which accounted for over 56% of total car sales in India, as 
per industry estimates.
Amid this evolving landscape, the Bank reinforced its 
leadership position in the new car loan segment through 
a series of strategic and customer-centric initiatives. 
Our strengthened on-ground presence across key dealerships, 
enabled by enhanced manpower deployment, has significantly 
improved sourcing capabilities across major OEM channels. 
Strategic tie-ups with leading automobile manufacturers have 
facilitated instant in-principle loan sanctions at the point of 
vehicle booking, with the Bank commanding a dominant share 
in these emerging delivery channels.
The introduction of Digital Document Execution for 
existing-to-bank (ETB) customers has further streamlined the 
loan processing experience, enhancing speed, convenience, 
and customer satisfaction. Aligned with our commitment to 
sustainability, the Bank has actively promoted “Green Car 
Loans” for electric vehicles (EVs), offering concessional interest 
rate and extended repayment tenors. Dedicated financing 
programs and attractive schemes have been consistently 
deployed to accelerate the adoption of eco-friendly mobility 
solutions.
These focussed initiatives have translated into strong 
business performance. The Auto Loan portfolio recorded 
a robust year-on-year growth of ₹10,809 crore (8.50%). 
During FY 2026, the Bank disbursed ₹54,398 crore in Auto 
Loans. Further, through disciplined credit monitoring and 
proactive portfolio management, asset quality has remained 
best-in-class, with NPAs contained at an exceptionally low 
level of 0.43% as of 31.03.26. Driven by innovation, operational 
excellence, and a customer-first approach, the Bank has 
enabled more than 6.22 lakh customers to realise their 
aspiration of owning a vehicle during the year, reinforcing its 
position as a trusted partner in their journey.
b) Strategic Initiatives
 y Partnership with Top Developers - Your Bank is 
collaborating with top developers across India to 
increase ticket size and address the growing demand for 
premium apartments
 y Corporate Tie-Ups - A structured policy has been 
introduced to strengthen tie-ups with reputed corporates 
and Public Sector Units and offer home loan solutions to 
their employees
c) New Product Launches and Improvements
 y Hybrid variants (a combination of Term Loan and 
Overdraft) have been introduced for Home Loan and 
Personal Loan Against Property
 y Feature enhancements have made Builder Finance 
Scheme and Home Loan for Repairs and Renovation 
more customer-centric
 y Eligible Home Loan customers are provided with an 
in-principle approval for Car Loan
d) End-to-End Digitalisation
Your Bank is actively working towards end-to-end digitalisation 
of Home Loans. With various initiatives being underway, 
we expect the digitalisation journey to be completed in  
FY 2026-27.

Education Loans
Your Bank continues to be the largest Education Loan provider 
in India, commanding 32.94% market share among ASCBs, 
as of March 2026. During FY 2026, the Bank empowered 
1,76,180 students with financial assistance, totalling ₹19,938 
crore, of which 42.77% of loans were extended to girl students. 
To enhance access, quality and customer satisfaction, your 
Bank has undertaken several initiatives, as below: 
 y PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme: Enables collateral-free, 
guarantee-free loans for students admitted to 967 
identified Quality Higher Education Institutions (QHEI). 
 y Scholar Loan Scheme: Extended to a broader set 
of top-rated 61 institutions with relaxed norms and 
concessional interest rates. 
 y Global Ed-vantage Scheme: Provides customised 
loans to support students pursuing education at foreign 
universities with relaxed terms. Your Bank offers collateral 
free loans of up to ₹50 lakh to students seeking admission 
in top 100 global institutions at competitive interest rates
 y Digital Document Execution: This was rolled out 
for unsecured Education Loans to improve borrower 
convenience and enable ease of credit flow to students 
 y In September 2025, your Bank also launched lifetime 
relationship calling through the contact centre. 
Customer receive calls at half yearly intervals during the 
study period and quarterly intervals during the repayment 
period to update them on various product/process 
related information
Through these focussed efforts, your Bank continues to 
support the aspirations of India’s youth and reinforce its 
leadership in Education Loans. 
Personal Loans (eXC)
Your Bank caters to the needs of the salaried class 
(Government, Defence and Private), and non-salaried 
customers through this product. SBI Personal Loans (erst. 
Xpress Credit) has reached ₹3,76,003 crore as on 31.03.2026. 
During this financial year, your Bank provided these loans to 
28 lakh customers amounting to ₹2,58,000 crore.
Your Bank recently increased the maximum quantum of 
these loans to ₹50 lakh. We are also extending these loans 
to ‘Agniveers’ wherein the loan amount of up to ₹5 lakh is 
made available to eligible customers for a maximum period 
of 3.5 years. Your Bank has implemented Digital Document 
Execution for SBI Personal Loans (erst. Xpress Credit) which 
leads to real-time execution of loan documents through 
e-stamping and e-signature. So far, this facility has been 
extended in 21 states and 5 Union Terrotories (UTs), and as 
on 31.03.2026, a total of 16,05,051 Personal Loan documents 
have been executed through this mode.
Pension Loans
Your Bank serves the needs of pensioners under the Pension 
Loan scheme. The Bank’s Pension Loan portfolio has grown 
to ₹64,025 crore as on 31.03.2026. During this financial year, 
the Bank sanctioned Pension Loans of ₹27,547 crore to  
6.74+ lakh customers.
To make the product more attractive and to enhance customer 
satisfaction, your Bank has undertaken the below steps:
 y Increased maximum loan amount up to ₹20 lakh 
 y Pre-Approved Pension Loan (PAPNL) can be availed 
digitally through YONO, INB and Contact Centre 
in 4 clicks only
Personal Gold Loan
Your Bank’s Gold Loan portfolio recorded a strong year-to-date 
growth of 111.51%, reaching ₹1,05,781 crore as of 31.03.2026. 
With this, it has empowered 35.46 lakh customers and helped 
them unlock the value of their idle gold for personal and 
financial needs. Additionally, overdraft Gold Loan product was 
launched for borrowers to cater their short-term credit needs.
With flexible loan tenures ranging from 3 to 36 months, the 
Bank continues to meet the customers’ varied requirements. 
Proactive monitoring and follow-up helped contain NPAs 
in Personal Gold Loans to ₹93.86 crore, representing just 
0.09% of the Gold Loan portfolio.
